channel.description: Latest articles from The Scranton Times-Tribune (thetimes-tribune.com)

item.title: Police: Scranton man endangered state parole officers
item.description: The 34-year-old was jailed after throwing an unknown substance on the ground that left a parole officer ill after handling it.

item.title: Shady Lane Cemetery work day
item.description: Abington Rotarian Anita Nealon, right, and her daughter Courtney demonstrated service above self as they recently volunteered at Shady Lane Cemetery’s work day. Cleanups are held periodically and are publicized.

item.title: COUNTERPOINT: Enforcing immigration law benefits Americans
item.description: The administration is right to argue that enforcing immigration laws gets criminal aliens out of communities.

item.title: POINT: Legal immigration boosts America’s innovation advantage
item.description: America’s economic strength rests on its ability to attract talent, reward hard work, and out-innovate global competitors.

item.title: Shapiro pitches more support for child care workers and student teachers. Home aides feel left out.
item.description: Early childhood educators and student teachers would see modest gains under the proposal, but the governor did not propose raises for home care workers.

item.title: Rotary Club of the Abingtons flag exchange
item.description: Rotary Club of the Abingtons President Chris Loftus exchanged club flags with Tim Genetti, the District 7410 governor, and James Baker, assistant district governor. Clubs display their own decorative flags at meetings and events. Rotarians traveling to other countries often take these flags showcasing local flair and global friendship.

item.title: : EditorialWe must protect Pennsylvania’s young people from chatbots
item.description: During Gov. Josh Shapiro’s lengthy and, on occasion, unusually partisan budget address this past Tuesday, one theme attracted significant support from both parties: preserving children and childhood from predatory technologies.

item.title: County awards contract for paving in Archbald, Jermyn
item.description: Lackawanna County commissioners recently awarded a roughly $700,000 contract for a paving project in Archbald and Jermyn.

item.title: HS BASKETBALL: Riverside boys, North Pocono girls end season as No. 1 teams
item.description: An exciting and extremely competitive high school basketball regular season concluded last week, and after all of the tight finishes and an extra game, the best rose to the top. The Riverside Vikings finished with a 21-1 record. The North Pocono Lady Trojans won a playoff game to claim the Lackawanna Division I championship last Saturday. They enter the postseason with a record of 18-4. Both teams are unanimous No. 1 selections in the final Times-Tribune High School Basketball Polls for the 2025

item.title: Starbucks, Chipotle projects progressing in Carbondale
item.description: Carbondale Mayor Michele Bannon said she anticipates construction for the projects will be completed by late spring or early summer.
